title: One rule for unplaceable references
summary: Replaces six overlapping reference rules (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start) with a single `unplaceable-reference` rule backed by a new candidate engine in `crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs`. The engine extracts Number, Phrase, Time and Name candidates from a paragraph, then decides whether the paragraph itself places each one (a link, a bracketed or colon description, a repository or file name, a known name, a definer sentence, an absolute date). Findings carry an `Evidence` value, and `osf-lint-core::resolve` now takes that evidence: statistical evidence (a guessed name, a quoted term) always resolves to Warning/Advise and can never refuse a reply, while deterministic findings keep the class-and-group matrix. A 66-fixture precision/recall harness and end-to-end stop-hook, commit-message and prompt-hook tests pin the behaviour.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared types and the level/remediation resolver that now consults a finding's evidence.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/hook.rs
nodes.summary: Reads the last assistant message from stdin and decides whether to refuse the reply. A new test pins that a reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is not refused.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Runs the writing lint over a commit message file. Its verify test now expects two errors, since the old chat-local rule and the new rule both fire until the old one is retired.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: osf hook prompt
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder shown on every prompt. A new end-to-end test asserts it never names one of the six retired rule ids.

nodes.label: Scan resolve-and-explain
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/scan/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves each scan finding's level and remediation, now passing the finding's own evidence into the shared resolver.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: The writing lint entry point. It now calls the new unplaceable_reference rule after undefined_names, and apply_context passes evidence through to the resolver for the new rule only.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/rules.rs
nodes.summary: The new rule. It gathers candidates per paragraph, picks one paragraph to report each repeated name from, and emits a finding for every candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: reference.rs
nodes.subtitle: candidate extraction
nodes.summary: The new 1831-line module. It finds Number, Phrase, Time and Name candidates, masks quoted and backticked spans, and keeps the longest candidate per kind when two overlap.

nodes.label: Placement judgment
nodes.subtitle: is_placed and helpers
nodes.summary: Decides whether a paragraph places a candidate: a link, a bracketed or colon description of two real words, a repository or file name in the same sentence, a known name, a definer sentence, or an absolute date.

nodes.label: names.rs
nodes.subtitle: known and generic words
nodes.summary: Adds is_generic_word and extends the built-in name list with frameworks, design systems and model tiers such as React, Vite, Sonnet and Opus.

nodes.label: Writing rule metadata
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: Adds the unplaceable-reference rule doc and threads Evidence through RuleMeta::resolve. Several example strings were reworded to avoid tripping the new rule.

nodes.label: resolve
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core/src/meta.rs
nodes.summary: The shared level-and-remediation resolver. It now takes an Evidence argument and returns Warning/Advise immediately for statistical evidence, before any class, group, context or exception is consulted.

nodes.label: Skill resolve-and-explain
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/skill.rs
nodes.summary: Passes each skill finding's evidence into the shared resolver, so a statistical skill finding is advisory too.

nodes.label: Unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: 66 labelled markdown files
nodes.summary: Each fixture carries an osf-unplaceable header naming its label, kind, target and reason. Placeable fixtures must yield no finding on the target; unplaceable ones must.

nodes.label: Precision/recall measure
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/unplaceable_measure.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over every fixture, tallies true and false positives and negatives per kind, and requires 100% precision and recall with no stray findings.

nodes.label: Checkpoint tests
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/unplaceable_checkpoints.rs
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests against the compiled binary: a bare fix number refuses the stop, a quoted example does not, and a relative time passes in a reply but fails a commit message.
